title: Cold-signal-driven soft-start and microburst autoscaler for Dedicated fleets
creator: Asha Raman
description:
Background:
Redwood Dedicated customers expect low tail latency for sudden bursts and short-lived spikes (microbursts). Existing warm-pool approaches load full model weights or eagerly hydrate KV caches for high-priority tenants, but they are costly at low utilization and slow to converge for unpredictable microburst patterns.

Goal:
Design and ship a lightweight, telemetry-driven 'Cold Signal Soft-Start' that reduces cold-start latency for small/medium microbursts while keeping warm-pool cost predictable. The feature should: (1) observe cold signals from routing/queueing layers and tenant traffic patterns, (2) make graded weight/kv preloads instead of full preheat, (3) perform a fast soft-start admission that allows limited concurrent microburst handling without full weight residency, and (4) integrate with autoscaler to scale up capacity if sustained.

Key components and approach:
- Cold signal detection: instrument LB/router to emit short-lived cold flags (e.g., request after >T_idle, cache miss rate >X) and produce a per-tenant cold-score time series (1s granularity).
- Soft-start download strategy: stream compact \"micro-slices\" of hot model layers (attention & embedding shards) via an incremental mmap-friendly slice format that can be memory-mapped and used for a conservative single-worker inference path. Full weights are loaded asynchronously only if load stabilizes.
- KV-diff priming: instead of seeding full KV cache, compute a small delta fingerprint (top-k recent prefixes for tenant) from historical traces and preseed only those KV entries to reduce prefix-miss penalty.
- Microburst admission controller: allow N_soft concurrent soft-start requests per node; use token-bucket tied to tenant commitment; soft-start requests use lower-priority compute lanes and bounded tokenized KV access to protect host SLOs.
- Autoscaler tie-in: if cold-score sustained across >M minutes or soft-start rejections exceed threshold, trigger quick scale-up path (microburst autoscale) with expedited node onboarding and prioritized weight streaming.
- Cost controls and fallback: track prefetch budget per tenant, stop preloads when budget exhausted, and fall back to warm-fallback models (smaller variant quantized) to preserve latency SLOs.

Acceptance criteria:
- 95th percentile cold-start tail reduced by >=40% for trial tenants with bursty workloads (simulated microbursts).
- Soft-start path must not increase stable-request latency on co-located tenants by more than 5% (measured on staging).
- Prefetch budget enforcement prevents uncontrolled memory/IO spikes during large churn.
- Integration tests validating correct autoscaler triggers and rollback behavior under noisy signals.

Telemetry and metrics:
- New metrics: tenant.cold_score, node.soft_start_inflight, tenant.prefetch_budget_used, soft_start_success_rate, kv_delta_hit_rate, microburst_autoscale_triggers.
- Dashboards: per-tenant cold heatmap, autoscale trigger timeline, prefetch IO and memory heatmap.
- Alerts: soft_start_success_rate < 80% for 5m, microburst_autoscale_triggers > 3 per hour for a single tenant without follow-up stabilization.

Design trade-offs and notes:
- Micro-slice loading trades safety for speed: we constrain the soft-start path to lower concurrency and simplified execution kernels to limit correctness risk. If a model produces out-of-spec results, requests must fail closed to avoid silent degradation.
- KV-diff priming relies on historical prefix signals; for completely novel tenants this yields limited benefit. Mitigation: seed with global hot-prefix set and fast cold re-evaluation.
- Storage/IO: incremental mmapped slices add complexity to weight packaging and node image layout; we will prototype as an optional sidecar streaming service to avoid changing current image format initially.

Implementation plan (high-level):
1) Instrumentation (1 sprint): add cold_score emission from router and basic dashboards.
2) Soft-start prototype (2 sprints): implement micro-slice stream format, in-node soft-start loader, and a guarded inference path.
3) KV-diff priming (1 sprint, parallel): build delta-index generator and small seeder; add budget accounting.
4) Admission controller + autoscaler hooks (1 sprint): tokenized admission and quick-scaler integration.
5) Canary + experiments (2 sprints): staged rollout on low-risk fleets, A/B test against baseline, adjust thresholds.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for micro-slice loader, admission token logic, and KV-diff algorithm.
- Integration test harness simulating microbursts with synthetic traffic (open-source toolkit) and measuring SLOs.
- Chaos tests: simulate failed slice downloads and ensure safe fallbacks.
- Performance bench: ensure soft-start path latency and CPU/memory overhead meet acceptance constraints.

Artifacts and links:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwoodinfra.internal/pages/COLD-SOFT-START (draft)
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rw-infra/pull/12846
- Autoscale hook RFC: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1_softstart_autoscale_rfc
- Dashboard mockup: https://dashboards.redwoodinfra.internal/d/soft-start/overview

Rollout plan:
- Phase 0: internal staging validation with synthetic tenants and canary traffic (2 weeks).
- Phase 1: opt-in alpha for selected Dedicated customers (3 weeks) with explicit prefetch budgets.
- Phase 2: broader gradual rollout with telemetry gating and adjustable budgets.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Slice format ownership: do infra archive teams prefer format-v1 (mmap-first) or a streaming-only sidecar? (Decision requested by 2026-03-20).
- Prefetch budget pricing: product to decide whether extra budget is billable or included in Dedicated SLAs.

Security and compliance notes:
- Soft-start slices contain model parameters; any new transport must support encryption-in-transit and KMS-signed manifests. Work with security to confirm signing and replay protections.

Next steps:
- Engineering: spike micro-slice prototype and router cold signal telemetry (owner: Luca).
- Product: confirm prefetch budget policy and alpha customers (owner: Maya Chen).
